key_finding.title: 981 seconds
key_finding.text: In Saffire VI, smoke was readily detected at 981 seconds, after most of the hazardous gas release had already happened.

gaps.text: There is currently no partial-gravity combustion data in PSI. Microgravity and normal-gravity results could bound what happens at intermediate gravity levels.

earth_use.title: Fine-water-mist extinguishers
earth_use.text: Developed for use on the ISS, with practical applications on Earth.

earth_use.title: Smoke detection
earth_use.text: A 1970s shuttle smoke detector that tells smoke from dust, giving fewer nuisance alarms. It has industrial uses, such as in mining.

earth_use.title: Firefighter air tanks
earth_use.text: Spacesuit technology adapted in the 1970s to improve firefighters' air tanks and breathing gear.

earth_use.title: Firefighter clothing
earth_use.text: Spacesuit technology applied in the 1980s to improve firefighter protective clothing.
earth_use.source_label: NASA Spinoff: New Technology for the Fire Attire

control_need.text: Detection came after most of the hazardous gas release, which suggests a need to detect gases earlier than smoke alone.
